title: Implementation: Staging Infra Handoff & Playbook Orientation
summary: Kickoff handoff from sales to CS/SE for staging infra and runbook orientation. Discussed VPC peering options, KMS/HSM key management, audit log retention, canary rollout strategy, and network egress. SE walked through playbook sections and staging run checklist. Action items: Redwood to share runbook draft, customer to provide CIDR ranges and SOC2 contact, schedule pilot smoke test in staging next week.
topics: Security: KMS, encryption at rest, audit logs
Next steps: pilot test, pricing/commits follow-up
action_items: Diego Patel: Share staging runbook draft and checklist (deadline: 2025-12-23)
Tom Keane: Provide VPC CIDR ranges, proxy egress whitelist, and NAT gateway details (deadline: 2025-12-20)
Maya Li: Create a canary rollout doc showing model pinning and fallback policy examples (deadline: 2025-12-22)
Priya Mehta: Share SOC 2 contact and required audit log retention window (deadline: 2025-12-21)
Ava Martinez: Send commercial recap and pilot pricing/options (deadline: 2025-12-19)
next_steps: Redwood to send staging runbook + access checklist
Customer to confirm network details and security contact
Schedule a 2-hour pilot smoke test during week of 2025-12-29
SE to provision a staging tenant and share temporary API key (scoped)
meeting_header: Date: 2025-12-18 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: 58 mins | Attendees: Ava, Diego, Maya (Redwood); Samira, Tom, Elijah, Priya, Jared (Ironclad Transit)
transcript:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining – well start in a sec once folks stop moving around, um this is the handoff from sales to CS and SE. quick intros?
[00:12] Samira Khan: Hi, Samira, head of eng at Ironclad. we've got Tom from infra, Elijah on product, Priya on security and Jared does SRE.
[00:18] Ava Martinez: Awesome. Diego, want to set the goal for today?
[00:22] Diego Patel: Yeah, goal is to walk through the staging infra handoff, confirm network and security must-haves, and align on the pilot smoke test next week. well also surface any blockers for private/dedicated later.
[00:33] Maya Li: Hey all, Maya, solutions eng. ill do the runbook walkthrough and show the canary example. note up front: this will be a staging-only provisioning, not prod until we clear audits.
[00:44] Tom Keane: Quick note, our staging is pretty locked down — corporate proxy, limited egress, and NAT per AZ; so we need specifics on ports and ip ranges.
[00:50] Maya Li: yep noted. our typical stack expects outbound to Redwood API endpoints on 443 and some telemetry to our observability endpoints. we can give an allowlist and a CIDR set.
[01:02] Priya Mehta: For security, we need to validate encryption key handling. do you support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM? and how are audit logs retained and exported?
[01:10] Maya Li: yes, we support customer-managed keys — KMS integration for hosted Private deployments; for Dedicated we can integrate with customer's KMS via our agent or HSM adapter. audit logs: default retention is 90 days; we can export to your S3 or syslog for longer retention.
[01:23] Samira Khan: Is there PII redaction baked in or is that on us?
[01:28] Diego Patel: We offer redaction helpers and masking at the application layer, but Redwoods run-time doesn't alter app payloads automatically. we recommend policies + evals to catch leakage.
[01:40] Elijah Ortiz: On rollouts — were concerned about model regressions. can you do canary by route and automatically fallback to previous model on quality drop?
[01:48] Maya Li: yes — our rollout policies support per-route model pinning and automatic fallback. you can set thresholds on latency and quality; quality checks tie into your eval sets or our built-in smoke prompts.
[02:01] Jared Cole: network latency is also a concern. What SLOs are typical for dedicated vs hosted?
[02:07] Maya Li: hosted typically hits 50-120ms for base generation on the models in our catalog under normal seq lengths; dedicated with pinned models and local GPU pools can get into 20-60ms depending on instance type. these are ballpark numbers.
[02:19] Tom Keane: okay useful. for staging we just need to validate functional flows. next: handoff checklist?
[02:25] Diego Patel: ill take you through that — first item: network connectivity requirements, well need CIDR ranges, egress proxies, and any firewall rules. second: user access and SSO mapping — do you want SCIM and SAML?
[02:38] Priya Mehta: Yes SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning. plus role-based access (ops vs dev). we need RBAC scoped to token usage and audit trails.
[02:46] Maya Li: we support SAML SSO and SCIM; tokens can be scoped by route and TTLs. audit trails include token-level request metadata.
[02:56] Samira Khan: how do we handle secrets? i.e., model keys and any credentials — can they live in our KMS only?
[03:03] Maya Li: for Private or Dedicated, key material can be kept in your KMS and well reference it. for hosted tenants we offer managed keys but can integrate with external KMS in many cases.
[03:12] Ava Martinez: quickly on commercials — well follow up via email but pilot terms are two weeks free credits and then a consumption estimate; ill send the exact note after.
[03:21] Tom Keane: cool. now walk the runbook.
[03:24] Maya Li: ok, open runbook section one: provisioning staging tenant — step 1: create staging project, step 2: VPC peering vs VPN — for folks behind corp proxy we typically recommend egress allowlist. step 3: provide CIDR and subnets. step 4: create scoped API key for the pilot.
[03:45] Samira Khan: does the scoped key allow us to limit models and routes?
[03:48] Maya Li: yes you can scope it to endpoints and set token TTL; this is useful for smoke tests only.
[03:55] [00:04:00] Diego Patel: s we also include health-check endpoints for the canary. se will set up a small traffic splitter for 10% canary.
[04:06] Maya Li: canary steps: 1) pin new model to route in canary mode; 2) run smoke prompts against holdout set; 3) check latency and quality thresholds; 4) promote if green, rollback if fail. we have a documented rollback play.
[04:25] Elijah Ortiz: How do we push evaluation metrics? is there a webhook?
[04:29] Maya Li: yes, we can push evaluation events to a webhook or to your datadog/new relic via our telemetry bridge.
[04:35] Tom Keane: about telemetry — what is the network egress for telemetry?
[04:38] Maya Li: telemetry goes to our observability endpoint over 443 by default; we can provide an option to forward to your S3 or syslog collector to avoid external egress.
[04:49] Priya Mehta: for compliance we need immutable audit logs for 1 year; is that possible?
[04:53] Maya Li: we can export logs to your S3 with object lock if you need WORM style retention; that would be part of the Private entitlements.
[05:02] [00:05:30] Samira Khan: on performance benchmarks — could we run a quick throughput test in staging? maybe a small bench job to measure p95?
[05:09] Maya Li: absolutely. we recommend using our benchmark harness; SE will coordinate and provide a script that runs synthetic sequences at different lengths and concurrency to measure latency/p95 and token cost.
[05:21] Jared Cole: any constraints re: KV cache or stateful session? we use conversational memory in a few flows.
[05:27] Maya Li: KV cache is supported, and you'll be able to control cache lifetimes. for stateful convo we recommend session tokens and tighten KV persistence in staging.
[05:38] Diego Patel: ill note that for the pilot were just validating flows not optimized cost. after the pilot Optimize can give batching/quantization suggestions.
[05:47] [00:06:00] Elijah Ortiz: question on data residency — for production we need EU data to stay in eu-west. how is region routing handled?
[06:00] Maya Li: routing policies let you pin region by customer. for hosted we have region variants; for Dedicated we can provision pools in your chosen region. we also have automated fallback if capacity in region is constrained, but that can be disabled for strict residency.
[06:14] Priya Mehta: ok important. also need to know about pen tests and SOC 2 evidence access.
[06:21] Ava Martinez: we have an SOC2 package and a pen test summary; ill attach the SOC2 report and the compliance matrix.
[06:28] Tom Keane: Great. next, staging access mechanics — what accounts do we need to create?
[06:32] Diego Patel: we typically ask for one admin SAML group for provisioning and a dedicated CI service account for automation. CI key should be scoped and TTL-limited.
[06:42] Samira Khan: we can create both. ill ask Tom to drop CIDR and service account details in the doc.
[06:47] [00:07:00] Maya Li: moving on: smoke test plan. step A: ingest 50 synthetic requests across common routes; step B: verify success rate > 98% and p95 under threshold; step C: run holdout eval for correctness. SE will provide the sample prompts.
[07:05] Jared Cole: who will run the smoke tests? Redwood or our SRE?
[07:08] Diego Patel: collaborative — SE will provide scripts, Redwood can run them first against staging tenant and then hand over the script to Ironclad to run as well.
[07:17] Samira Khan: timeline?
[07:19] Ava Martinez: propose pilot smoke for week of 12/29; Diego to schedule.
[07:23] Tom Keane: my only major blocker is getting proxy egress allowlist done fast.
[07:28] Diego Patel: noted — Tom to share those details by Friday 12/20.
[07:32] [00:08:00] Priya Mehta: minor question: encryption in transit — do you have mTLS for service-to-service?
[07:37] Maya Li: we support TLS 1.2/1.3 by default; mTLS can be enabled in Private deployments.
[07:43] Priya Mehta: ok add that to the action items.
[07:46] Samira Khan: any limits on model uploads or custom models?
[07:50] Maya Li: you can bring custom models in Private or Dedicated. Hosted has a vetting/curation step for model safety. model size limits depend on architecture but weve onboarded multi-gig checkpoints with quantization help.
[08:03] Elijah Ortiz: is there any extra latency if we enable KMS for each request?
[08:07] Maya Li: minimal — we cache key handles and only call KMS for key material exchange at session start; per-request latency impact is small with proper caching.
[08:17] [00:09:00] Tom Keane: can you remind us about fallback behavior if a region is down? will traffic shift globally?
[08:24] Maya Li: by default routing will prefer region and then fall back to a global pool if policy allows; for strict residency you can disable fallback.
[08:33] Ava Martinez: ill add that to the runbook notes: explicit flag to disable cross-region fallback.
[08:38] Diego Patel: quick callout on cost — dedicated reserved is more predictable but requires commit. Optimize service can recommend quantization/batching for your workload to hit lower unit costs.
[08:51] Samira Khan: for pilot were not committing; we want to validate ops and quality first.
[08:56] Diego Patel: understood.
[08:58] [00:10:00] Maya Li: next, incident playbook excerpt: detection, escalation, rollback. if canary fails quality thresholds, automatic rollback triggers and an incident is created with links to traces. we push alerts to your pagerduty integration.
[09:14] Jared Cole: ok, do you have runbook templates we can copy into our internal runbooks?
[09:18] Maya Li: yes, SE will share markdown templates — startup checklist, rollback, and run escalation matrix.
[09:24] Samira Khan: great. im curious about rate limiting — if our prod traffic spikes how do you protect models?
[09:31] Maya Li: we have per-route rate limits and token bucket policies; for dedicated capacity you can set guaranteed throughput and a burst queue.
[09:40] Tom Keane: totally. my ops question: during onboarding will there be a test load that simulates our peak?
[09:46] Diego Patel: yes, we can run a scaled bench job but wed need accurate concurrency numbers — Tom, can you provide expected peak rps and seq length distributions?
[09:55] Tom Keane: yep ill add to the doc.
[09:58] [00:11:00] Ava Martinez: were about halfway through; any other security blockers?
[11:03] Priya Mehta: just access to SOC2 and a pen test addendum — and a contact to run a pre-prod tabletop if needed.
[11:10] Ava Martinez: ill attach SOC2 and Diego will introduce the security contact.
[11:15] Maya Li: also note: if you want HSM-backed signing for model artifacts we can enable that for Private.
[11:21] Samira Khan: interesting, please include details.
[11:24] [00:12:00] Elijah Ortiz: product-level: can we add a post-deploy eval step that runs NLU accuracy checks on a sample set and posts results to a dashboard?
[11:33] Maya Li: yes, we can hook evals into the pipeline; results can be published to your dashboard or to our console and linked to alerts for regressions.
[11:41] Diego Patel: action: Maya to create canary doc and eval webhook example.
[11:45] Maya Li: noted.
[11:48] [00:13:00] Samira Khan: anything about data deletion — if we need to remove staging artifacts quickly?
[11:53] Maya Li: yes deletions can be requested via support; for Private you have self-service controls to purge data and logs. we keep a deletion audit trail.
[12:03] Jared Cole: good. slack channel preference — do we have a dedicated Redwood <> Ironclad channel?
[12:07] Ava Martinez: we can set one up; ill invite the named attendees and Diego will join.
[12:12] Tom Keane: that helps.
[12:15] [00:14:00] Diego Patel: recap quick: Redwood sends runbook and SOC2; Ironclad sends CIDR, proxy and service account details; SE shares canary and benchmark scripts; schedule pilot week of 12/29.
[12:28] Samira Khan: sounds good; one ask — can we get a short recorded walkthrough video of the runbook?
[12:33] Maya Li: yes can do a 10-15 minute screen share and ill upload it.
[12:37] Priya Mehta: thanks, thats useful for our audit log.
[12:41] [00:15:00] Ava Martinez: any final questions?
[12:44] Tom Keane: onboarding checklist item: who is our escalation contact at Redwood during the pilot?
[12:49] Diego Patel: primary contact is me (Diego). secondary is Maya for SE technical issues and Ava for account.
[12:57] Elijah Ortiz: ok, please include PagerDuty integration notes as well.
[13:01] Maya Li: will do.
[13:04] [00:16:00] Samira Khan: thanks all — well aim to have the network details to you by 12/20 and expect Diegos runbook the next day.
[13:13] Diego Patel: great; ill send that today and target 12/23 for the draft runbook.
[13:18] Ava Martinez: ill send the commercial recap and SOC2 after the call.
[13:22] [00:17:00] Maya Li: one more technical note — if Ironclad wants to test quantized models we can provide a quantization profile and guidance for lower-cost inference.
[13:30] Samira Khan: were interested in that post-pilot.
[13:34] Priya Mehta: quick compliance question later: if we need a contractual addendum for longer log retention, how long does negotiation usually take?
[13:41] Ava Martinez: typical addenda are 2-3 weeks once requirements are specified; ill loop in legal.
[13:47] [00:18:00] Diego Patel: ok last part — scheduling: ill follow up with a Doodle for the 2-hour smoke test window.
[13:55] Tom Keane: fine.
[13:57] [00:19:00] Ava Martinez: thanks everyone, well close with a quick recap in the follow-up email.
[14:03] Samira Khan: thanks.
[14:06] [00:20:00] -- call ends with logistics and note of recorded session --

Notes about transcript: occasional transcription errors present (e.g., non-standard capitalization, misheard product names). timestamps are approximate every 30-90s.
